summary: Tested the 3 new features (mandatory campaign name, drip/Daily Sending Limit, Template Name (Your Reference)) end-to-end. Backend: new pytest suite /app/backend/tests/test_drip_and_campaign_name.py — 11/11 passed (blank/whitespace campaignName -> 400, drip without perDay -> 400, drip > account dailyLimit (2000) -> 400, drip == limit allowed, drip start-now -> processing with dripEnabled/dripDailyLimit/dripStartAt in /lite, drip future start -> scheduled with scheduledAt==dripStartAt, non-drip + scheduled regressions, no _id leaks). Frontend (Playwright, real UI as QA user): campaign-name-required-note + disabled send with empty name; saved-template load auto-fills template-reference-input; drip-toggle reveals drip-settings; estimate correct (20@5/day -> 'finish in 4 days', 20@3/day -> 'finish in 7 days'); 5000/day shows drip-limit-warning, hides estimate and keeps send disabled; schedule-toggle disabled + schedule-disabled-note; drip campaign created -> Campaign Details shows campaign-template-reference, campaign-template-name, 'Daily Sending Limit: 5 messages/day • 3 day(s) left', 'Next Daily Batch Aug 30 05:57' and status scheduled after first 5-message window (5 failed at BizChat as expected with dummy creds, 15 pending); future-start drip stays scheduled with 0 sent; non-drip campaign shows '—' reference and no drip block. No console errors, no API 5xx.

design_issues.screen: Send Messages – Daily Sending Limit card
issues: drip-start-input uses min={new Date().toISOString().slice(0,16)} which is a UTC string while the input is local time — in negative-UTC-offset timezones this blocks valid near-future local times (and in positive offsets allows slightly-past times). Same pre-existing pattern on schedule-datetime. Cosmetic/validation-only; backend accepts and normalises.

critical_code_review_comments: routes/messages.py send_messages(): for drip campaigns the response reports dailyUsage = current usage + dripDailyLimit before anything is actually sent — cosmetic but slightly misleading if ever surfaced in a toast (the drip toast currently ignores it).
SendMessagesSimple.js: drip start-time min uses UTC ISO instead of local — use a local-time formatted min string for datetime-local inputs.
